d: Administrative area of nine states used by INPE since 1988. It is not the same as the polygon of the Amazon biome.
Period from August 1 to July 31, used by INPE to measure deforestation. It does not coincide with the calendar year.
Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados (National Data Protection Authority). Federal agency that oversees compliance with the Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados.
Area assigned by the public authorities to agrarian reform families.
Annual publication by Ipea with the FBSP that calculates homicide rates per 100,000 inhabitants from SUS death records.

A record that a macro-topic is not dealt with in the document. It describes the coverage of the text, not the position of the candidacy. It is not a quotation and does not enter the quotation count — it has a count of its own, because it carries no passage and no page.
Partido Avante. Founded in 1989 as Partido Trabalhista do Brasil (PTdoB), it adopted its current name in 2017.
ex: Partido de Augusto Cury nesta eleição.

d: Banco Central do Brasil (Central Bank of Brazil). Monetary authority: it sets the policy interest rate through the Copom, regulates the financial system and publishes the fiscal and credit statistics used on this page.
Online betting houses, regulated in Brazil starting in 2023.
Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (National Bank for Economic and Social Development). Federal public bank for long-term financing.
Federal cash transfer program created in 2003. It was called Auxílio Brasil between 2021 and 2023, when it returned to its previous name and design, with revised rules.

Benefício de Prestação Continuada (Continuous Cash Benefit). One monthly minimum wage paid to low-income elderly people and to people with disabilities who meet the income test. It is a right set out in the Constitution, not a government program.
Cooperation group of Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, expanded since 2024.
Cadastro Único para Programas Sociais (Single Registry for Social Programs). Registry of low-income families that gives access to Bolsa Família, to BPC and to other programs.
Caixa Econômica Federal. Federal public bank; it operates the FGTS, housing finance and the payment of a large share of social benefits.
Sum of everything the federal government, the states and the municipalities collect in taxes, divided by GDP. It measures the weight of the system on the economy, not the tax paid by a family.
Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (Contribution on Goods and Services). Federal tax created by the 2023 tax reform to replace PIS, Cofins and IPI.
Count of the entire population carried out by IBGE, in principle every ten years. The most recent was the Censo 2022.
Controladoria-Geral da União (Office of the Comptroller General of the Union). Internal oversight body of the federal government.

Classificação Internacional de Doenças, 10ª revisão (International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision). Standard code that defines what a person died of in death records. Homicides correspond to codes X85 to Y09.
Contribuição de Intervenção no Domínio Econômico (Contribution for Intervention in the Economic Domain) levied on fuels, created in 2001.
The basic unit of this study: an excerpt from a government plan, with the page it came from and the classification of that excerpt.
Contribuição para o Financiamento da Seguridade Social (Contribution for the Financing of Social Security). Federal tax on companies' revenue.
Raw materials traded on international markets at standardized prices — soybeans, iron ore, oil. The upswing in these prices is called the commodities boom.
Set of rules and internal controls to ensure that an organization complies with the law.
Comitê de Política Monetária (Monetary Policy Committee) of the Banco Central. It meets every 45 days and sets the target for the Selic rate.
Complete removal of the forest cover of an area, which is what PRODES measures.
Contribuição Provisória sobre Movimentação Financeira. Levied on bank transactions between 1997 and 2007, when the Senate rejected its extension.
Physical facility that houses computing servers and data storage.
Departamento de Informática do SUS (SUS Information Technology Department). It publishes the public health databases, among them the Sistema de Informações sobre Mortalidade (SIM).

A person who would like to work and would be available, but stopped looking because they believe they would not find a job. Since looking for work is part of the definition of unemployed, they are NOT counted in the unemployment rate.
Quotation that states a direction without allowing that verification. It is not worse than a proposal — it is another type of text.
Name of the Banco Central's digital currency project.
Everything the public sector owes, without netting out what it has to receive. Measured as a percentage of GDP.
Gross debt minus the public sector's credits — international reserves and claims on public banks, among others. It is systematically lower than gross debt and measures something else.
Change to the text of the Constitution. It requires three-fifths of the votes in two rounds, in the Chamber of Deputies and in the Senate.

Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (National Secondary Education Exam). Test administered by INEP since 1998; since 2009 the score has been calculated using Item Response Theory, which makes earlier scores incomparable with current ones.
Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública (Brazilian Public Security Forum). Civil society organization that publishes the Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública and, with Ipea, the Atlas da Violência.
Fundo de Garantia do Tempo de Serviço (Severance Pay Guarantee Fund). Monthly deposit made by the employer into the worker's account.
Company that offers financial services built on technology, outside the traditional banking structure.
Sum of employed and unemployed people. It is the denominator of the unemployment rate.
The labor force plus the potential labor force. It is the denominator of the underutilisation rate, and that is why this rate is always higher than the unemployment rate.
Fundação Nacional dos Povos Indígenas (National Foundation of Indigenous Peoples). Federal agency responsible for indigenous policy, including land demarcation.
Score from 1 to 5 for how much information the sentence carries about what exactly will be done. It measures the text, not the merit of the policy.
Final step in the demarcation of an indigenous land, carried out by presidential decree.
Point of concentration and redistribution — of flights, of cargo or of data.

Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics). It produces the Censo, the GDP figures, the IPCA, the INPC and the PNAD. Most of the series on this page come from it.
Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (Tax on Goods and Services). State and municipal tax created by the 2023 tax reform to replace ICMS and ISS.
Imposto sobre Circulação de Mercadorias e Serviços (Tax on the Circulation of Goods and Services). Main state tax.
Índice de Desenvolvimento da Educação Básica (Basic Education Development Index). It combines the Prova Brasil score with the pass rate, on a scale of 0 to 10. Calculated every two years.
Federal tax created by the 2023 reform to apply to goods and services deemed harmful to health or to the environment.
Instituto Nacional de Colonização e Reforma Agrária (National Institute for Colonization and Agrarian Reform). It carries out the policy of land settlements and land titling.
Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Anísio Teixeira National Institute for Educational Studies and Research). It administers the Enem and calculates the Ideb.

Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor (National Consumer Price Index). The same price collection as the IPCA, but with the consumption basket of households earning 1 to 5 minimum wages — where food, transportation and energy carry more weight.
Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (National Institute for Space Research). It monitors deforestation by satellite through the PRODES and DETER systems.
Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (National Social Security Institute). Agency that grants and pays retirement benefits, pensions and the BPC.
Imposto sobre Operações Financeiras. It is levied on credit, foreign exchange, insurance and securities; its rates can be changed by decree, without going through Congress.

Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo (Broad National Consumer Price Index). The country's official inflation index, the benchmark for the target pursued by the Banco Central. It covers households with incomes from 1 to 40 minimum wages.
Instituto de Pesquisa Econômica Aplicada (Institute for Applied Economic Research). Public research foundation linked to the federal government; it publishes, with the FBSP, the Atlas da Violência.
Imposto sobre Produtos Industrializados (Tax on Industrialized Products). Federal tax on industrial production.
Imposto Sobre Serviços (Tax on Services). Main municipal tax.
Imposto sobre Valor Agregado (Value Added Tax). Model in which the tax applies only to the value added at each stage. CBS and IBS together form the Brazilian IVA.
Law that regulates provisions of the Constitution and requires an absolute majority to be approved.
Each of the 20 subjects into which the quotations were organized.
Digital platform where multiple sellers offer products to buyers.
Movimento Brasil Livre. A political movement founded in 2014; it is not a registered party. Renan Santos is one of its founders.

Movimento Democrático Brasileiro (Brazilian Democratic Movement). Heir to the tolerated opposition party of the military dictatorship; it was called PMDB between 1980 and 2017, when it returned to its original name.

Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome (Ministry of Social Development and Assistance, Family and Fight against Hunger). Responsible for Bolsa Família and for BPC.
Microempreendedor Individual (Individual Microentrepreneur). Simplified formalization regime created in 2008 for self-employed workers.
Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos (Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services). It publishes the annual report on federal state-owned companies.
Partido Missão. Party label under which Renan Santos is running in this election.
Medida Provisória (Provisional Measure). Act with force of law issued by the president, which lapses if Congress does not approve it within the deadline.
Partido Novo (New Party). Founded in 2011 and registered in 2015, with a liberal economic platform. Romeu Zema's party.
Regime in which a company deducts from the tax due what was already paid at earlier stages of the chain — it prevents tax from being levied on tax.

Organização para a Cooperação e Desenvolvimento Econômico (Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development). Group of countries that standardizes economic statistics; Brazil is not a full member.
Company or account established outside the country of residence of whoever controls it.
Difference between two percentages. Going from 60% to 65% is a rise of 5 percentage points — not of 5%.
Partido Patriota. Name adopted in 2018 by the former PEN; it merged into the PTB in 2023, forming the PRD.
Partido da Causa Operária (Workers' Cause Party). Founded in 1995, Trotskyist in orientation. Rui Costa Pimenta's party.
Partido Democrático Trabalhista (Democratic Labor Party). Founded in 1979 by Leonel Brizola.
Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (Proposed Constitutional Amendment). It is the bill that, if approved, becomes a Constitutional Amendment.
Polícia Federal (Federal Police).

Programa de Integração Social e Programa de Formação do Patrimônio do Servidor Público (Social Integration Program and Public Servant Asset Formation Program). Federal contributions on companies' revenue.
Instant payment system of the Banco Central, in operation since November 2020.
Partido Liberal (Liberal Party). Current name of the former PR, adopted in 2019. Flávio Bolsonaro's party.
Name of the MDB between 1980 and 2017. It appears in old affiliation records.
Pesquisa Mensal de Emprego. The IBGE employment survey used until 2015; it covered only six metropolitan regions, and for that reason its numbers are not comparable with those of the PNAD Contínua.
Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios (National Household Sample Survey). Annual IBGE survey, discontinued in 2015.
Survey that replaced the PNAD starting in 2012. It covers the entire national territory and is released each quarter. It is the source of the unemployment rate used today.
Progressistas. Successor to the PPB and, before it, to the PPR and the PDS.
Partido Progressista Brasileiro (Brazilian Progressive Party), later Partido Progressista (Progressive Party). Acronym that appears in party affiliations prior to 2003.

Programa de Cálculo do Desflorestamento da Amazônia (Amazon Deforestation Calculation Program), run by INPE. It measures by satellite the clear-cutting of forest in each crop year, from August to July.
Quotation in which, reading only what is written, it is possible to say yes or no about compliance by the end of the term.
Partido Republicano da Ordem Social (Republican Party of the Social Order). Founded in 2010; absorbed into Solidariedade in 2023.
Partido Renovador Trabalhista Brasileiro (Brazilian Labor Renewal Party). Founded in 1994. Pablo Marçal's party.
Geological layer beneath a thick band of salt on the seabed, where the largest oil reserves discovered in the country lie, starting in 2006.
Partido Socialista Brasileiro (Brazilian Socialist Party). Refounded in 1985.
Partido Social Cristão (Social Christian Party). Founded in 1985.
Partido Social Democrático (Social Democratic Party). Founded in 2011. Ronaldo Caiado's party.
Partido da Social Democracia Brasileira (Brazilian Social Democracy Party). Founded in 1988; it was Fernando Henrique Cardoso's party.
Partido Social Liberal (Social Liberal Party). Founded in 1994; it merged with the DEM in 2022, giving rise to União Brasil.
Partido dos Trabalhadores (Workers' Party). Founded in 1980. Party of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and of Dilma Rousseff.
Value already adjusted for inflation to a reference date, which makes it possible to compare different years.
Value in the money of the year itself, with no correction for inflation. Comparing current reais from distant years understates the older value.
Secretaria Especial da Receita Federal do Brasil (Special Secretariat of the Federal Revenue of Brazil). It collects federal taxes and publishes the annual tax burden report.
Update of a survey's sample weights when the population estimate changes. IBGE rebased the PNAD Contínua in 2025 based on the Censo 2022.
Partido Republicanos. Name adopted in 2019 by the former PRB.
Difference between government revenue and spending, not counting interest on the debt. It is the measure of the year's fiscal effort.
Payment owed to the owner of a resource or of a right for its use — in the case of oil, to the federal government, the states and the producing municipalities.
The economy's policy interest rate, set by the Copom. It serves as a floor for the cost of money in the country.
Secretaria Especial de Saúde Indígena (Special Secretariat of Indigenous Health), of the Ministério da Saúde. Responsible for the Distritos Sanitários Especiais Indígenas.
Sistema Gerenciador de Séries Temporais (Time Series Management System) of the Banco Central. Public database from which the interest rate, exchange rate and debt series cited here come.
Sistema IBGE de Recuperação Automática (IBGE Automatic Retrieval System). Public database holding IBGE's tables; the table codes cited on this page point there.
Sistema de Informações sobre Mortalidade (Mortality Information System), of the Ministério da Saúde. It records every death in the country and is the basis for homicide rates.
Sistema de Informações de Projetos de Reforma Agrária (Agrarian Reform Project Information System), of INCRA.
Partido Solidariedade. Founded in 2013, originating in the Força Sindical trade union federation.
Difference between the bank's cost of funding and the interest charged to the borrower.
New company, generally technology-based, looking for a business model that can grow quickly.
Supremo Tribunal Federal. The country's constitutional court; its eleven justices are nominated by the president and approved by the Senate.
Superior Tribunal de Justiça (Superior Court of Justice). Last instance for non-constitutional cases.
Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional (National Treasury Secretariat). It manages the federal public debt and publishes the central government's fiscal statistics.
Situation of someone who works fewer than 40 hours a week, would like to work more and is available to do so.
Sistema Único de Saúde (Unified Health System). Public health system created by the 1988 Constitution, with universal and free access.
Broadest IBGE indicator: it adds unemployed people, workers underemployed due to insufficient hours and the potential labor force, over the expanded labor force.
Share of the labor force that is out of work, looked for a job in the last 30 days and was available to start. It is what is popularly called the unemployment rate.
Tribunal de Contas da União (Federal Court of Accounts). External oversight body, auxiliary to Congress.

Fiscal rule established by Constitutional Amendment 95, of 2016, which capped the growth of primary spending at the previous year's inflation. Replaced in 2023 by the Novo Regime Fiscal (New Fiscal Framework).
A transcription is the literal text of the document, checked by script. A paraphrase is a summary written by whoever extracted it — and in that case, what counts is what is in the PDF.
Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (Superior Electoral Court). It organizes the elections, registers candidacies and publishes the candidates' asset declarations.
Document that transfers full ownership of the plot to the settler. Different from a concession of use, which does not transfer ownership.
Unidade da Federação (Federative Unit). The 26 states plus the Federal District.
Party resulting from the merger of DEM and PSL, registered in 2022.
Venture capital: investment in young companies with high growth potential and a high chance of failure.
Word for word. Here it indicates that the excerpt was checked character by character against the text of the PDF on the page cited.
Open data dashboard of the Ministério do Desenvolvimento Social, with the figures for Bolsa Família and BPC.
From the English year to date: the accumulated total for the year so far. A YTD figure is not the year's final result.
